packages.name: vm_service
packages.description: A library to communicate with a service implementing the Dart VM service protocol.
packages.oneLiner: A library to communicate with a service implementing the Dart VM service protocol.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a Dart client library to communicate with the Dart VM service protocol. It allows developers to interact with running Dart and Flutter virtual machines for debugging and inspection purposes.
useWhen: Building debugging tools or developer extensions for Dart and Flutter
Interacting directly with the Dart VM service protocol programmatically
avoidWhen: Building standard application features unrelated to debugging or VM inspection
strengths: Official library for communicating with the Dart VM service
Kept up-to-date with Dart VM service protocol specifications
weaknesses: Low-level protocol client which requires deep understanding of the Dart VM service spec

packages.name: analyzer
packages.description: This package provides a library that performs static analysis of Dart code.
packages.oneLiner: Performs static analysis of Dart code for tool integration and embedding.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a library for performing static analysis on Dart code. It allows developers to configure analysis options, examine elements, and build custom IDE tools, formatters, or documentation generators.
useWhen: You are building a custom Dart tool or editor integration
You need to programmatically analyze Dart source code and inspect elements
avoidWhen: You just want to run standard linting on your project (use the built-in `dart analyze` command instead)
You are an end-user looking for a command-line analysis tool
strengths: Powers major Dart tooling like dart format and dart doc
Supports fine-grained analysis options and custom lint rules
weaknesses: APIs were originally machine generated from a Java implementation and may not feel like clean Dart APIs
No clean distinction currently between public and internal APIs, leading to potential breaking changes
explainer.setupNotes: Add the dependency to pubspec.yaml and optionally configure an analysis_options.yaml file in your project root.

packages.name: archive
packages.description: Provides encoders and decoders for various archive and compression formats such as zip, tar, bzip2, gzip, zlib, xz, and zstd.
packages.oneLiner: Encodes and decodes archive and compression formats such as zip, tar, gzip, and zlib.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides encoders and decoders for various archive and compression formats. It handles reading and writing zip, tar, bzip2, gzip, zlib, xz, and zstd formats both in memory and via streaming.
useWhen: You need to read or write zip and tar archives within a Dart or Flutter app.
You need to decompress or compress data using formats like GZip, ZLib, BZip2, XZ, or Zstandard.
avoidWhen: You are running on the web platform and need to use InputFileStream for local file system access.
strengths: Supports a wide variety of compression and archive formats.
Provides stream-based APIs and memory-efficient file streaming to minimize memory usage.
weaknesses: File system operations like InputFileStream are not supported on the web platform.

packages.name: yaml
packages.description: A parser for YAML, a human-friendly data serialization standard
packages.oneLiner: A Dart library for parsing YAML documents into Dart data structures.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides functions to load YAML strings or streams into Dart objects. It supports error recovery and detailed error reporting. The library does not support dumping YAML back to text.
useWhen: Parsing configuration files in Dart or Flutter apps
Converting YAML data to Dart maps/lists for further processing
Reading YAML from network or local files
avoidWhen: When you need to generate YAML output
When working with very large YAML files that require streaming parsing
strengths: Pure Dart implementation, no native dependencies
Supports error recovery with custom listeners
Maintained by dart-lang with regular updates
Compatible with all platforms (web, mobile, desktop)
weaknesses: No YAML dumping support
Limited to parsing, not editing or serializing
Some edge cases (self-referential collections) still throw exceptions

packages.name: meta
packages.description: Annotations used to express developer intentions that can't otherwise be deduced by statically analyzing source code.
packages.oneLiner: Annotations to express developer intentions for static analysis tools.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides annotations like @visibleForTesting, @immutable, and @sealed that static analysis tools use to analyze source code and check developer intentions. It also includes experimental annotations for dart2js.
useWhen: You want to guide the Dart analyzer with custom metadata on classes, methods, or variables.
You are writing code that requires strict enforcement of architectural intentions such as mustCallSuper or immutable.
avoidWhen: You need a general-purpose state management or UI library.
You are looking for runtime dependency injection frameworks.
strengths: Officially maintained by the Dart team.
Zero dependencies.
Directly integrates with the Dart analyzer and IDE warnings.
weaknesses: Provides only annotations and no runtime logic or utilities.
Some hints/annotations may be experimental or change between minor versions.
explainer.setupNotes: Add package to dependencies in pubspec.yaml.

packages.name: pub_semver
packages.description: Versions and version constraints implementing pub's versioning policy. This is very similar to vanilla semver, with a few corner cases.
packages.oneLiner: Versions and version constraints implementing pub's versioning policy.

explainer.whatItDoes: Implements parsing, comparison, and constraint checking for semantic version numbers according to pub's specific versioning policy. It handles special pub corner cases like build suffix ordering and pre-release prioritization.
useWhen: You need to parse and compare semantic version numbers in Dart
You are building tools that deal with pub-compatible package version constraints
avoidWhen: You are looking for vanilla semver without pub's specific pre-release and build suffix policies
strengths: Matches pub's exact versioning and constraint policy
Handles complex ranges, unions, and pre-release priority rules
weaknesses: Not strictly compliant with vanilla SemVer 2.0.0 in certain corner cases due to pub-specific policies

packages.name: uuid
packages.description: RFC4122 (v1, v4, v5, v6, v7, v8) UUID Generator and Parser for Dart
packages.oneLiner: Generates and parses RFC‑4122/9562 UUIDs (v1‑v8) for Dart.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides functions to create version‑1,‑4,‑5,‑6,‑7 and‑8 UUIDs and to validate or parse 128‑bit hexadecimal strings. Works on all Dart platforms with cryptographically strong RNG by default.
useWhen: You need unique identifiers across devices or services
You require support for newer UUID versions (v6‑v8) or strict RFC validation
avoidWhen: You need a UUID library with built‑in persistence or database integration
You prefer a code‑gen based solution for IDs
strengths: Cryptographically strong random generation on all platforms
Supports the full range of RFC‑4122 and RFC‑9562 versions
Provides explicit format validation and parsing utilities
weaknesses: Only focuses on UUID generation/parsing – no storage or networking features
No code‑generation helpers; you must call the API directly

packages.name: mime
packages.description: Utilities for handling media (MIME) types, including determining a type from a file extension and file contents.
packages.oneLiner: Utilities to resolve MIME types from file names, magic bytes, and to parse multipart streams.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides functions to look up a MIME type based on a filename or header bytes and to get a file extension from a MIME type. Includes a stream transformer that splits multipart/form-data into separate parts.
useWhen: You need to determine MIME types for files without external libraries
You need to parse multipart/form-data streams in a server or client
You want a lightweight, pure‑Dart solution for MIME handling
avoidWhen: You require a full‑featured HTTP client that already handles multipart parsing
You need advanced MIME type detection beyond extensions and basic magic numbers
strengths: Zero dependencies, pure Dart
Supports both extension and magic‑byte lookup
Provides a ready‑to‑use multipart stream transformer
weaknesses: Limited to the built‑in MIME table; not exhaustive for obscure types
No async API for large file scanning beyond header bytes

packages.name: stack_trace
packages.description: A package for manipulating stack traces and printing them readably.
packages.oneLiner: Provides parsing, inspection, and readable formatting of Dart stack traces.

explainer.whatItDoes: The package can convert native StackTrace objects into Trace objects, format them into human‑readable strings, and capture asynchronous stack chains. It also offers utilities like terse formatting to collapse core library frames.
useWhen: You need clearer error logs during development or production debugging
You want to track asynchronous call stacks across zones
You need to format stack traces for reporting or logging
avoidWhen: You only need simple stack traces and want to avoid extra dependencies
Your app size constraints are extremely tight and you cannot afford any extra package
strengths: Produces concise, readable stack traces
Supports asynchronous stack chain capture
Works on all Dart platforms
No code generation required
weaknesses: Adds runtime overhead when capturing chains
Limited to stack‑trace manipulation; not a full logging solution

alternatives.name: logging
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides general logging facilities but lacks stack‑trace parsing and chain features

packages.name: crypto
packages.description: Implementations of SHA, MD5, and HMAC cryptographic functions.
packages.oneLiner: Provides SHA, MD5, and HMAC hashing functions for Dart.

explainer.whatItDoes: Implements common cryptographic hash algorithms (SHA‑1/224/256/384/512, MD5) and HMAC support. All code is pure Dart and works on every Flutter platform.
useWhen: You need to compute hashes or HMACs locally in a Dart/Flutter app.
You require a lightweight, pure‑Dart solution without native dependencies.
avoidWhen: You need audited, security‑certified cryptography.
You require algorithms not provided (e.g., Argon2, RSA).
strengths: Pure Dart, no native dependencies
Supports a wide range of hash functions and HMAC
Works on all Flutter platforms
Performance improvements in recent versions
weaknesses: Not reviewed by security professionals
Limited to hashing/HMAC, no encryption or key management
May lack the latest cryptographic primitives

packages.name: glob
packages.description: A library to perform Bash-style file and directory globbing.
packages.oneLiner: A file and directory globbing library that supports Bash-style path matching and listing.

explainer.whatItDoes: Performs Bash-style file and directory globbing in Dart. It allows developers to check whether a path matches a specific pattern, or recursively list filesystem entities matching a glob pattern using POSIX path syntax.
useWhen: You need to filter files or paths using wildcards like `*` or `**`
You want to recursively list files in a directory matching specific extensions or patterns
avoidWhen: You only need basic path manipulation provided natively by `package:path`
You need complex recursive directory traversal without glob pattern matching
strengths: Supports familiar Bash-style glob syntax including wildcards, character ranges, and option expansion
Works consistently across cross-platform environments using POSIX path syntax
Integrates seamlessly with `package:file` for filesystem operations
weaknesses: Combinatorial option expansions exceeding 10,000 branches will throw a FormatException
Requires using specific imports or a FileSystem object for filesystem listing APIs since version 2.0.0
explainer.setupNotes: none

packages.name: xml
packages.description: Full-featured XML for Dart — DOM parsing, SAX streaming, XPath 3 querying, and a fluent builder API.
packages.oneLiner: Full-featured XML and XPath library for DOM parsing, SAX streaming, and fluent building.

explainer.whatItDoes: Dart XML provides tools for parsing, traversing, querying via XPath 3.1, and building XML documents. It supports both in-memory DOM manipulation and memory-efficient event-driven SAX streaming.
useWhen: You need to parse, query, or manipulate XML documents in Dart or Flutter.
You require XPath 3.1 support for complex document queries.
You need to process large XML streams efficiently without buffering the entire tree.
avoidWhen: You need strict XML Schema (XSD) validation built directly into the parser.
You require full XSLT transformations or complex XQuery modules.
strengths: Comprehensive W3C XPath 3.1 implementation and DOM model.
Supports both pull- and push-based event-driven SAX streaming.
Zero overhead and fully portable across Dart VM, Flutter, and Web.
weaknesses: Does not validate documents against XML Schema (XSD) definitions.
External DTD entity resolution and validation are not enforced.

packages.name: package_config
packages.description: Support for reading and writing Dart Package Configuration files.
packages.oneLiner: Read and write Dart package configuration files.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides APIs to locate, read, and write .dart_tool/package_config.json files. Offers discovery functions and typed models for package configurations. No longer supports legacy .packages files.
useWhen: You need to resolve package URIs in tooling or build scripts
You are building a Dart tool that must read or modify the package configuration
avoidWhen: You only need simple path manipulation without package resolution
Your project targets Dart versions older than 3.4
strengths: Official API that follows the Dart package config spec
Discovery functions simplify locating config files
Typed models are sealed and ready for future immutability
weaknesses: Only handles package configuration, not a general utility library
Requires Dart 3.4+, so not usable on older SDKs

packages.name: built_value
packages.description: Value types with builders, Dart classes as enums, and serialization. This library is the runtime dependency.
packages.oneLiner: Immutable value types with builders, enum classes and JSON serialization for Dart.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a runtime library to define immutable data models using the builder pattern. Supports enum‑like classes and full JSON (de)serialization, working together with built_collection.
useWhen: You need strongly typed, immutable models with builders
You require robust JSON serialization that handles generics and nested built collections
You want enum‑style classes with additional behavior
avoidWhen: You prefer a lightweight solution without code generation
Your project is small and a simple json_serializable approach is sufficient
strengths: Zero‑runtime reflection – fast and safe
Full support for generics, nested built collections, and custom serializers
Builder pattern enforces immutability and safe updates
weaknesses: Requires build_runner and a generator dev dependency
Steeper learning curve compared to plain json_serializable
Adds extra build step to the CI pipeline
explainer.setupNotes: Add built_value_generator and build_runner as dev_dependencies, then run `dart run build_runner build` (or watch).

alternatives.name: freezed
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides similar immutable data classes with union types and less boilerplate

alternatives.name: json_serializable
alternatives.why_pick_it: Simpler code‑gen for JSON (de)serialization without the builder pattern

packages.name: io
packages.description: Utilities for the Dart VM Runtime including support for ANSI colors, file copying, and standard exit code values.
packages.oneLiner: Utilities for the Dart VM Runtime including ANSI colors, file copying, and exit code values.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides helper utilities for Dart VM applications such as ANSI color wrappers for terminal output, file path copying functions, a process manager for spawning subprocesses, and a subscriber-safe wrapper around standard input.
useWhen: You are building a command-line interface (CLI) or Dart VM script that needs terminal colors.
You need to spawn and manage external processes with forwarded I/O streams.
You need to copy directory trees recursively or check if files are executable.
avoidWhen: You are building a Flutter mobile or web application where CLI terminal utilities and process spawning are not applicable.
strengths: Simplifies working with command-line processes and standard input streams.
Provides built-in ANSI coloring helpers for terminal output.
Includes recursive file and directory copying utilities.
weaknesses: Limited to Dart VM environments and does not apply to standard Flutter UI development.
Small feature set focused strictly on specific VM utilities.

packages.name: pool
packages.description: Manage a finite pool of resources. Useful for controlling concurrent file system or network requests.
packages.oneLiner: Manage a finite pool of resources to control concurrent operations.

explainer.whatItDoes: The pool package exposes a Pool class that makes it easy to manage a limited pool of resources. It controls concurrent file system or network requests through withResource or fine-grained PoolResource management.
useWhen: You need to limit concurrent file system or network requests.
You want to process an iterable asynchronously with a maximum concurrency limit.
avoidWhen: You are managing state or UI components.
You do not need to limit concurrency.
strengths: Easy to use with withResource callbacks.
Supports fine-grained control via PoolResource objects.
Includes deadlock timeout handling.
weaknesses: Requires manual tracking to ensure physical resources correspond correctly to pool allocations.

packages.name: dart_style
packages.description: Opinionated, automatic Dart source code formatter. Provides an API and a CLI tool.
packages.oneLiner: Provides an API and CLI to format Dart source code automatically.

explainer.whatItDoes: Rewrites Dart code to follow the official Dart style guide, handling indentation, line wrapping, and punctuation. It can be used as a library or via the `dart format` command.
useWhen: Enforcing consistent code style in a project
Running formatting in CI or pre‑commit hooks
avoidWhen: Needing runtime code transformation
When you require linting beyond formatting
strengths: Official package from the Dart team
Works with the Dart SDK `dart format` command
Configurable via analysis options
weaknesses: Only formats code, no linting or analysis
Limited configuration options

packages.name: platform
packages.description: A pluggable, mockable platform information abstraction for Dart.
packages.oneLiner: Cross‑platform abstraction for querying runtime platform info in Dart.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a unified API to access native and web platform details, with mock support for tests. It wraps dart:io Platform on native runtimes and exposes browser data on the web.
useWhen: Need to detect OS or browser in a single API
Require testable platform mocks
Build apps that run on multiple Dart platforms without conditional imports
avoidWhen: You only target a single platform and want minimal dependencies
You need advanced device features beyond basic platform info
strengths: Simple, zero‑dependency API
Built‑in test mocking
Supports all major Dart platforms
No code generation required
weaknesses: Limited to platform info only, no device capabilities
Requires manual null checks for web vs native
API changes in 3.2.0 may need migration

alternatives.name: plugin_platform_interface
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides a base for platform interfaces but requires custom implementation

alternatives.name: browser_launcher
alternatives.why_pick_it: Only for web browser detection, not cross‑platform

packages.name: petitparser
packages.description: Build fast, composable, and type-safe grammars and parsers in Dart.
packages.oneLiner: Build fast, composable, and type-safe grammars and parsers in plain Dart code.

explainer.whatItDoes: PetitParser allows developers to build small, specialized parsers directly in plain Dart code and combine them like LEGO bricks to parse text, configuration values, or complex programming languages. It provides type-safe combinators, character predicates, and transformation methods without requiring external code generators or fragile regular expressions.
useWhen: You need to parse custom text formats, configuration files, or DSLs directly in Dart.
You want a type-safe and composable alternative to complex regular expressions.
You want to build and test grammars in-memory without a separate code-generation step.
avoidWhen: You are parsing simple JSON or formats with widely available dedicated serializers.
You prefer external generator tools (like ANTLR) over code-as-grammar libraries.
strengths: Fully type-safe using modern Dart features and records.
Highly composable with a rich set of combinators and builders.
No external code generators required.
Built-in tools for debugging and viewing execution trees.
weaknesses: Steeper learning curve for developers unfamiliar with parser combinators.
May be overkill for trivial string manipulation tasks.

packages.name: clock
packages.description: A fakeable wrapper for dart:core clock APIs.
packages.oneLiner: A fakeable wrapper for dart:core clock APIs.

explainer.whatItDoes: Encapsulates the notion of the current time using a Clock class. Allows swapping out the default top-level clock to reliably test timing-dependent code.
useWhen: You need to test timing-dependent code reliably
You want to mock time or use fake_async for tests
avoidWhen: You only need standard DateTime functionality without mocking or testing requirements
strengths: Integrates seamlessly with the fake_async package
Provides a top-level clock field for default usage
weaknesses: Requires using the wrapper instead of direct dart:core DateTime calls

packages.name: async
packages.description: Utility functions and classes related to the 'dart:async' library.
packages.oneLiner: Utility classes and helpers that extend Dart's async library.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides wrappers, transformers, and helpers for Futures, Streams, and async operations such as caching, memoizing, cancelable operations, and stream grouping. Includes convenience classes like RestartableTimer and Result.
useWhen: You need advanced stream manipulation or cancellation support
You want to cache or memoize expensive async results
avoidWhen: You only need simple async without extra helpers
You require a full state‑management solution
strengths: Rich set of async utilities
Well‑maintained by Dart team
Works on all Dart platforms
weaknesses: Adds extra abstraction layer
May be overkill for tiny projects

packages.name: coverage
packages.description: Coverage data manipulation and formatting
packages.oneLiner: Collects, manipulates, and formats code coverage data in Dart

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides tools to collect coverage JSON from the Dart VM Service and format it into LCOV or pretty-printed formats. Supports ignoring specific lines or ranges from coverage and handling function or branch coverage.
useWhen: You need to generate lcov.info files for test coverage reporting
You want to collect coverage data from the Dart VM Service
You need to filter out ignored lines using coverage comments
avoidWhen: You are looking for a state management or UI library
You do not need test coverage metrics for your Dart project
strengths: Supports LCOV and pretty-printed format output
Supports function and branch coverage collection
Provides comment directives to ignore lines or files from coverage
weaknesses: Web coverage percentage metrics and line counts are not directly comparable to VM runs
explainer.setupNotes: Run dart pub global activate coverage and optionally add the executables to your PATH.
explainer.example: dart pub global run coverage:test_with_coverage

packages.name: source_span
packages.description: Provides a standard representation for source code locations and spans.
packages.oneLiner: Standard representation for source code locations, spans, and human-friendly error messages.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides classes like SourceSpan and SourceFile to track positions in source code files. It allows packages to easily pass code locations around and generate clear, human-friendly error messages with line and column highlights.
useWhen: You are writing a parser, compiler, linter, or code generator that needs to report source code errors.
You want to standardize source location tracking across multiple custom packages.
avoidWhen: You are building a standard mobile application UI without any code parsing requirements.
strengths: Generates clean, human-friendly error messages with file context and line numbers.
Efficient means of computing line and column numbers using SourceFile.
Supports multi-span highlights and Unicode box-drawing characters.
weaknesses: Very niche utility package with no application outside of parsing and tooling.

packages.name: pubspec_parse
packages.description: Simple package for parsing pubspec.yaml files with a type-safe API and rich error reporting.
packages.oneLiner: Parse pubspec.yaml files with a type‑safe API and detailed error reporting.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides classes to read and write pubspec.yaml content, exposing hosted, git, and path dependencies as typed objects. Supports lenient parsing, preserves map spans, and can serialize back to a Map.
useWhen: You need to validate or transform a pubspec.yaml in a tool or CI step
You are building a CLI that inspects package metadata
You want a robust, typed representation of pubspec fields for analysis
avoidWhen: Parsing arbitrary YAML where a generic parser is sufficient
Runtime pubspec parsing in a production Flutter app where size matters
strengths: Typed API for all pubspec fields
Rich, precise error messages via checked_yaml
Supports latest Dart pubspec features (git tag_pattern, falseSecrets, hooks, platforms)
Lenient mode to ignore unknown keys
weaknesses: Specialized to pubspec files only, not a general YAML library
No code‑generation support
Adds another dependency if you already use a generic YAML parser

alternatives.name: yaml
alternatives.why_pick_it: A generic YAML parser that can read any YAML file, including pubspec.yaml, without extra package overhead

packages.name: test_api
packages.description: The user facing API for structuring Dart tests and checking expectations.
packages.oneLiner: The user facing API for structuring Dart tests and checking expectations.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides core APIs for writing and structuring tests in Dart. It supplies the foundational definitions for tests, groups, and expectations.
useWhen: You are building testing tools or libraries that need to hook into the test execution structure.
avoidWhen: You are writing standard unit or integration tests for a Dart or Flutter application (use package:test instead).
strengths: Provides the underlying API required to structure tests and check expectations.
Actively maintained and versioned alongside core testing infrastructure.
weaknesses: Not intended to be publicly used directly for standard application testing.
API may take time to stabilize according to the documentation.

alternatives.name: test
alternatives.why_pick_it: Package:test is the standard and intended package to use for writing and running Dart tests.

packages.name: ffi
packages.description: Utilities for working with Foreign Function Interface (FFI) code.
packages.oneLiner: Utilities for working with Foreign Function Interface (FFI) code in Dart.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides utility functions and classes for working with Foreign Function Interface (FFI) code. It includes capabilities for converting between Dart strings and C strings encoded with UTF-8 and UTF-16.
useWhen: You need to interoperate with C libraries from Dart
You need to handle UTF-8 and UTF-16 string conversions for C interop
avoidWhen: You are writing pure Dart code without native C integration
strengths: Official utility package for Dart FFI string and memory handling
Simplifies conversion between Dart strings and C strings
weaknesses: Requires understanding of native memory management and FFI concepts
explainer.setupNotes: Not documented
explainer.example:
import 'package:ffi/ffi.dart';

// Allocate and free native memory or convert strings using package utilities.

packages.name: hooks
packages.description: A library that contains a Dart API for the JSON-based protocol for `hook/build.dart` and `hook/link.dart`.
packages.oneLiner: Dart API for the JSON-based protocol for package build and link hooks.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a Dart library for writing `hook/build.dart` and `hook/link.dart` scripts to automate building or gathering assets and performing whole-application optimization.
useWhen: You are building or gathering code assets or native binaries for a Dart package
You need to run custom build tasks during a Dart build via hook scripts
avoidWhen: You are developing standard pure-Dart packages that do not require native asset compilation or hooks
strengths: Standardized protocol for native assets and hooks in Dart
Supports user-defines configuration from pubspec.yaml
weaknesses: Niche package restricted to native asset and hook workflows
explainer.setupNotes: Requires setting up build and link scripts within the `hook/` directory of your Dart package.

packages.name: json_annotation
packages.description: Classes and helper functions that support JSON code generation via the `json_serializable` package.
packages.oneLiner: Provides annotations for json_serializable to generate JSON (de)serialization code.

explainer.whatItDoes: Defines annotation classes like @JsonSerializable and @JsonKey that json_serializable reads to produce boilerplate for converting Dart objects to and from JSON. It does not contain any runtime logic itself.
useWhen: You need compile‑time JSON (de)serialization without writing manual toJson/fromJson code.
You are already using json_serializable or want a lightweight annotation package.
avoidWhen: You prefer runtime reflection‑based JSON handling (e.g., json_annotation is not needed).
You target platforms where code generation is not possible.
strengths: Small, zero‑runtime‑overhead package.
Works with Dart 3 and newer SDKs.
Provides fine‑grained control via JsonKey options.

avoidWhen: You can easily construct real instances or tested fake implementations for your tests.

packages.oneLiner: Common utility classes for Strings, Dates, X509, PKCS, Cryptography and HTTP requests.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a collection of helper classes for common string operations, domain and email validation, cryptographic functions, X509 certificates, PKCS12 files, and basic HTTP operations.
useWhen: You need helper functions for string manipulation, math operations, or color utilities.
Your application deals with X509 certificates, CSR generation, or cryptographic operations in pure Dart.
You need simple HTTP request helpers or DNS lookup utilities.
avoidWhen: You only need a specific well-maintained library for cryptography or networking and want to avoid a broad utility dependency.
strengths: Wide variety of helper classes in a single package ranging from strings to crypto and X509 certificates.
Pure Dart package compatible with all platforms including web, mobile, and desktop.
weaknesses: Monolithic utility packages can lead to unused code if only a small subset of features is required.

packages.name: jiffy
packages.description: Jiffy is a Flutter (Android, IOS and Web) date time package for parsing, manipulating, querying and formatting dates and time
packages.oneLiner: Parse, manipulate, query, and format dates and times in Dart and Flutter.

explainer.whatItDoes: Jiffy is a date time package for Flutter and Dart that simplifies parsing strings, lists, or maps into dates, manipulating them through additions or subtractions, querying relationships like 'isBefore' or 'isBetween', and formatting with custom patterns or relative time strings.
useWhen: You need complex date calculations and time manipulation in your app
You require relative time formatting like '5 years ago' or 'in 25 years
You want easy localized date formatting across multiple languages
avoidWhen: You only need basic DateTime operations provided natively by Dart
You want a reactive or stream-based clock library
strengths: Extensive formatting options and pre-set formats
Robust relative time calculations (from/to now)
Built-in localization support for multiple locales
weaknesses: Adds an external dependency for features overlapping with the standard library
Requires asynchronous loading/setting for non-default locales
explainer.setupNotes: Simply add jiffy to your pubspec.yaml dependencies and import it.

packages.name: mcp_dart
packages.description: Dart and Flutter SDK for building Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, clients, hosts, and AI tools.
packages.oneLiner: Dart and Flutter SDK for building Model Context Protocol clients, servers, and AI tools.

explainer.whatItDoes: Implements the Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification to build servers, clients, and hosts that connect AI models to tools, resources, and prompts. It supports multiple transports including stdio, Streamable HTTP, and IO streams, alongside OAuth authentication hooks.
useWhen: You need to build a custom Model Context Protocol server or client in Dart or Flutter.
You want to expose Dart tools, resources, and prompts to AI agents via MCP.
avoidWhen: You prefer the official Dart team ai package (dart_mcp) over this implementation.
You are not using the Model Context Protocol.
strengths: Implements complete core client/server wire requirements for MCP specifications.
Supports multiple transports including stdio, Streamable HTTP, and custom streams across various platforms.
weaknesses: Optional extensions like Tasks are not part of official core conformance claims.
Requires careful configuration for large messages or specific HTTP transport limits.
explainer.setupNotes: Add the package using `dart pub add mcp_dart` or configure it via version constraints in pubspec.yaml.

packages.name: talker
packages.description: Advanced error handler and logger package for flutter and dart. App monitoring, logs history, report sharing, custom logs, and etc.
packages.oneLiner: Advanced error handler and logger package for Flutter and Dart apps.

explainer.whatItDoes: Talker provides logging, error and exception handling, app monitoring, log history, report sharing, and custom logs for Flutter and Dart. It offers built-in support for network calls and state management libraries through companion packages.
useWhen: You need structured logging and error handling across your Flutter or Dart app
You want a UI screen to monitor logs and errors directly on the device
You need to catch, share, and report exceptions and app actions
avoidWhen: You only need a simple, single-line console logger without history or reporting
You are building a lightweight CLI utility where a heavy error monitoring toolkit is unnecessary
strengths: Comprehensive log history and report sharing capabilities
Extensive integrations for Dio, HTTP, BLoC, Riverpod, Chopper, and gRPC
Customizable log formats, colors, and titles
weaknesses: Requires using multiple companion packages (like talker_flutter, talker_dio_logger) for full feature sets across the ecosystem
Can add overhead if only basic print statements are needed
explainer.setupNotes: Simply add talker to your pubspec.yaml and instantiate Talker().

alternatives.name: logger
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick logger if you only need a simple, zero-setup pretty console logger without history tracking or advanced monitoring UI features.

alternatives.name: sentry
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick sentry if your primary goal is cloud-based crash reporting rather than local debugging and custom log filtering.

packages.name: signature
packages.description: A Flutter plugin providing performance optimized signature canvas with ability to set custom style, boundaries and initial state.
packages.oneLiner: A Flutter plugin providing a performance-optimized signature canvas with custom styling and export.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a signature canvas widget and a controller for capturing user signatures. Allows customizing stroke width, pen color, and background, as well as exporting the drawing to PNG or SVG bytes, or restoring from previously saved points.
useWhen: You need users to draw signatures on screen in a Flutter application.
You need to export signatures as PNG or SVG images.
You need undo/redo functionality for canvas drawing.
avoidWhen: You are building a complex freehand drawing or painting app requiring multi-layer support or brushes.
You do not need signature capture functionality.
strengths: Performance optimized for a wide range of devices.
Supports exporting drawings to PNG and SVG formats.
Includes built-in undo, redo, and initial state restoration.
weaknesses: Limited to single-layer signature input and basic canvas manipulation.
Requires manual wrapping in an Expanded widget inside flex layouts when used without explicit dimensions.

packages.name: flutter_quill_delta_from_html
packages.description: Convert easily HTML inputs content to Quill Js Delta format
packages.oneLiner: Converts HTML strings to Quill Delta format for use with Quill editor.

explainer.whatItDoes: This package parses HTML input and produces a list of Quill Delta operations that represent the same content. It supports a wide range of HTML tags, CSS styles, and custom block handlers.
useWhen: Importing HTML content into a Quill editor
Migrating web‑based rich text to a Flutter app
Creating custom block embeds from HTML
avoidWhen: You need a full HTML renderer or editor that works directly with HTML
The content contains complex table layouts beyond basic support
strengths: Wide tag and CSS support, including line‑height, colors, and text formatting
Custom block handling via CustomHtmlPart
No build_runner or code generation required
weaknesses: Basic table support only, may not handle complex tables
No direct support for rendering HTML, only conversion to Delta

packages.name: quill_native_bridge
packages.description: An internal Flutter plugin for flutter_quill package to access platform-specific APIs
packages.oneLiner: An internal plugin for flutter_quill to access platform-specific clipboard and gallery APIs

useWhen: You are using flutter_quill and need platform-specific clipboard and media operations
You need to read or write HTML, images, and files to the system clipboard across multiple platforms
avoidWhen: You are not using flutter_quill and need standard clipboard or file picking capabilities
You need general-purpose device information rather than quill-specific platform integrations
strengths: Cross-platform support for advanced clipboard types like HTML, images, and GIFs
Direct integration with flutter_quill package requirements
weaknesses: Intended as an internal package for flutter_quill rather than standalone general use
Requires platform-specific configuration such as FileProvider on Android and Photo Library permissions on iOS and macOS
explainer.setupNotes: Requires Android FileProvider configuration for clipboard image sharing, and Photo Library usage descriptions in Info.plist for iOS/macOS image saving.
explainer.example: final String? html = await QuillNativeBridge().getClipboardHtml();

packages.oneLiner: Save files from bytes, paths, streams, and URLs across Android, iOS, Web, Windows, macOS, and Linux.

packages.name: flutter_rating_bar
packages.description: A simple yet fully customizable ratingbar for flutter which also include a rating bar indicator, supporting any fraction of rating.
packages.oneLiner: A fully customizable rating bar and indicator widget supporting fractions and vertical layout.

You need an interactive star or custom icon rating input in forms.
avoidWhen: You need complex non-rating input form elements like sliders or date pickers.

Supports fractional ratings and vertical or horizontal orientations.
Includes a rating bar indicator for read-only displays.
weaknesses: Limited to rating-related use cases.

packages.name: home_widget
packages.description: A plugin to provide a common interface for creating HomeScreen Widgets for Android and iOS.
packages.oneLiner: Plugin to send data to native home screen widgets on Android and iOS

useWhen: You need to display dynamic content on the device home screen
You want to update the widget from Flutter code
You need to support both Android and iOS home screen widgets
avoidWhen: You want to render Flutter widgets directly on the home screen
You need a fully declarative widget system without native code
strengths: Unified cross‑platform API

Handles null values and baseline alignment

No Flutter widgets can be rendered on the home screen

packages.name: audio_service
packages.description: Flutter plugin to play audio in the background while the screen is off.
packages.oneLiner: Flutter plugin for background audio playback with media controls.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a way to run audio code in the background while the screen is off. It exposes a standard AudioHandler API that forwards media actions to your own player implementation and updates system notifications, lock screen, headset buttons and Android Auto/Apple CarPlay.
useWhen: You need background audio that continues when the app is minimized or the screen is locked
You want system media controls, notifications, lock‑screen or Android Auto integration
You need a unified API that works on Android, iOS, web and macOS
avoidWhen: Your app only plays short foreground sounds and doesn’t need background playback
You prefer a zero‑native‑code solution for simple audio
You already use a full‑featured media player that handles its own background service
strengths: Full platform support (Android, iOS, web, macOS, Linux via MPRIS)
Works with any audio engine (just_audio, flutter_tts, etc.)
Rich feature set: queue, shuffle, repeat, custom actions, lock‑screen UI
weaknesses: Requires native configuration (Android manifest, iOS background modes)
Adds complexity compared to plain audio players
May be overkill for simple use‑cases
explainer.setupNotes: Add Android permissions and notification channel in AndroidManifest.xml, enable Background Modes (Audio) in Xcode, configure AudioServiceConfig with channel IDs, and ensure a compatible audio player (e.g., just_audio) is used inside the AudioHandler.

packages.name: mutex
packages.description: Mutual exclusion with implementation of normal and read-write mutex
packages.oneLiner: Mutual exclusion locks and read-write locks for asynchronous Dart code

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides normal mutex and read-write mutex implementations to protect critical sections of code and prevent race conditions when using asynchronous operations. Includes convenience methods like protect, protectRead, and protectWrite to safely acquire and release locks.
useWhen: You have asynchronous operations inside critical sections that risk race conditions
You need multiple read locks to exist simultaneously while restricting write locks to a single exclusive instance
avoidWhen: Your critical section only contains synchronous code, which cannot be interrupted in Dart
Your critical section does not involve shared data or resources accessible by other asynchronous code
strengths: Supports both normal mutexes and read-write mutexes
Convenience methods ensure locks are always released correctly via try-finally blocks
weaknesses: Requires proper management to avoid deadlocks in complex asynchronous flows

packages.name: rx
packages.description: Reactive Extensions Library for Dart providing an API for asynchronous programming with observable streams.
packages.oneLiner: Reactive Extensions library for Dart offering observable streams and async operators.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a set of observable types, subjects, and operators for composing asynchronous data flows. Includes converters to and from Dart Streams and Futures, plus experimental reactive values.
useWhen: You need fine‑grained control over async data pipelines
You prefer Rx‑style operators over native Stream methods
You want a lightweight, pure‑Dart reactive library
avoidWhen: You require a full state‑management solution
You need code‑generation based APIs
strengths: Rich set of operators and subjects
Works without depending on Dart Stream API
Well‑tested and documented
weaknesses: Experimental; may lack some Rx features
Requires Dart 3.8+
No built‑in state‑management integration

packages.name: easy_localization
packages.description: Easy and Fast internationalizing and localization your Flutter Apps, this package simplify the internationalizing process .
packages.oneLiner: Easy and fast Flutter internationalization with JSON/CSV/… loaders

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a simple API to load translation files from assets or custom loaders, supports plural, gender, nesting, RTL and fallback locales, and offers extension methods on Text and BuildContext.
useWhen: You need a quick, zero‑boilerplate solution for localizing a Flutter app
You want to load translations from JSON, CSV, Yaml, or XML files
You need runtime locale switching with persistence
You want code generation for translation keys
avoidWhen: You already use a full‑featured i18n framework like intl or slang
You need advanced features like message formatting with ICU or custom plural rules beyond what intl offers
You want to avoid adding an assets folder to your project

Built‑in fallback and error handling
Code generation for keys
weaknesses: Requires assets folder and iOS plist configuration
Limited to Flutter (no pure Dart support)
Not as feature‑rich as intl for complex formatting

alternatives.name: intl

alternatives.name: slang

packages.oneLiner: A rich text WYSIWYG editor component and toolbar for Flutter apps.

You want to store and manipulate text documents using Quill Delta JSON format.
avoidWhen: You only need simple single-line or multi-line plain text inputs.
You want to natively store documents primarily as HTML or Markdown without conversion packages.

Extensible embed blocks and toolbar options.

weaknesses: Storing documents directly as HTML requires additional community conversion packages.

packages.name: flutter_contacts
packages.description: Fast, complete contact management for Android, iOS & macOS — all fields, groups, accounts, vCards, native dialogs, listeners, SIM contacts, and number blocking.
packages.oneLiner: Fast native contacts management for Android, iOS, and macOS.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides CRUD operations for contacts, accounts, groups, vCard import/export, and change listeners. It supports native dialogs and platform-specific capabilities such as SIM contacts and ringtones.
useWhen: You need to read, write, or manage device contacts across Android, iOS, and macOS.
You require fast bulk operations for large contact lists.
avoidWhen: You only need cross-platform storage that does not integrate with native system contacts.
You are targeting web or platforms other than Android, iOS, and macOS.

Comprehensive property support and native dialog integration.
weaknesses: Requires platform-specific permissions setup.
Certain features (like SIM contacts or blocked numbers) are restricted to Android.

packages.name: git

packages.oneLiner: Git command line wrapper for inspecting and manipulating local Git repositories.

Cross-platform support across Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux

Limited to local repository operations

packages.name: flutter_webrtc
packages.description: Flutter WebRTC plugin for iOS/Android/Desktop/Web, based on GoogleWebRTC.
packages.oneLiner: WebRTC plugin for real-time audio, video and data communication.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides WebRTC APIs for Flutter applications across mobile, desktop, and web platforms. Enables peer-to-peer audio/video streaming, data channels, and screen capture using native GoogleWebRTC bindings.

Implementing peer-to-peer data channels for multiplayer games or file sharing
Sharing screen contents across mobile and desktop platforms
avoidWhen: You only need simple media playback from URLs without peer-to-peer streaming
You want a fully managed video backend without setting up signaling servers

Actively maintained with regular updates to the underlying libwebrtc SDK

Complex API surface inherent to the WebRTC specification

packages.name: flutter_hooks
packages.description: A flutter implementation of React hooks. It adds a new kind of widget with enhanced code reuse.
packages.oneLiner: A Flutter implementation of React hooks for managing widget life-cycle and code reuse.

explainer.whatItDoes: It introduces a new kind of object (hooks) that manage the life-cycle of a widget, allowing you to extract and share stateful logic like AnimationControllers across widgets without using complex mixins.
useWhen: You want to share stateful logic across multiple widgets without boilerplate.
You prefer a hooks-based architecture similar to React inside Flutter's build methods.
avoidWhen: You rely heavily on standard StatefulWidget structures and do not want to adopt a hooks paradigm.

Extracted logic can be easily packaged and published independently.
weaknesses: Requires strict adherence to rules (calling hooks unconditionally and prefixing with 'use').

packages.name: back_button_interceptor
packages.description: Back Button Interceptor. May be used to do stuff when the Android back-button is tapped, as an alternative to `WillPopScope`.
packages.oneLiner: Intercept Android back-button taps with custom functions as an alternative to WillPopScope.

explainer.whatItDoes: Allows developers to add custom interceptor functions that are executed when the device's back button is tapped. If any interceptor returns true, the default navigation pop action is prevented. Functions can be ordered using z-indexes and named for easy removal.
useWhen: You need custom handling when the Android back button is pressed within stateful widgets.
You want an alternative to WillPopScope with support for multiple ordered interceptors.
avoidWhen: You are using deep links with the GoRouter package, as it is currently incompatible.
You are relying strictly on standard declarative navigation routing without custom back handling.
strengths: Supports multiple ordered interceptors via z-index and registration order.
Allows both synchronous and asynchronous interceptor functions.
Provides test-friendly methods to simulate back button presses and inspect results.
weaknesses: Incompatible with GoRouter deep links.
Requires manual removal of interceptors in the dispose method to avoid memory leaks.
explainer.setupNotes: To make it work on Android 13 and up, set android:enableOnBackInvokedCallback="false" in the Android manifest.

explainer.setupNotes: Add as dev_dependency, run `dart pub add --dev build_web_compilers`, create a build.yaml with entrypoint builder configuration, and run `dart run build_runner build`
explainer.example:
```yaml
# build.yaml
targets:
  $default:
    builders:
      build_web_compilers:entrypoint:
        generate_for:
          - web/**.dart
        options:
          compilers:
            dart2js:
              args:
                - O2
            dart2wasm:
              args:
                - O3
```

useWhen: You need to validate structured data against a JSON Schema in a Dart/Flutter app
You want a standard‑compliant schema builder without writing raw JSON
You need synchronous validation for performance or offline use
avoidWhen: You only need simple type checks and prefer built‑in Dart validation
You are already using a code‑generation approach for JSON models
strengths: Full Draft 2020‑12 support
Fluent, type‑safe API
Synchronous validation path
Rich error reporting
weaknesses: No code generation integration
Requires manual schema construction
Not a UI form builder

packages.name: form_builder_validators
packages.description: Form Builder Validators set of validators for FlutterFormBuilder. Provides common validators and a way to make your own.
packages.oneLiner: A comprehensive collection of ready-made FormField validators for Flutter.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides standard validation rules (like required, email, numeric, credit card, etc.) for any FormField widget. It allows combining multiple validation rules, transforming values, and localizing error messages into numerous languages.
useWhen: You need pre-built validators for common input types like email, URLs, numbers, and custom regex.
You need to internationalize form error messages into multiple languages.
You want to compose or chain multiple validation rules together declaratively.
avoidWhen: You are using a state-management form library that already has its own robust validation mechanism like formz and prefer keeping validation tied directly to that model.

Built-in localization support for dozens of languages.
Supports composing, conditional validation, and chaining validators.
weaknesses: Requires maintaining additional dependencies if used for very basic forms where standard Flutter validator callbacks suffice.

alternatives.name: formz
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose formz if you prefer a standalone, immutable input validation approach for BLoC or other state management solutions without relying on Flutter's FormField widgets.

alternatives.name: string_validator

explainer.example:
TextFormField(

)

packages.name: amplify_auth_cognito
packages.description: The Amplify Flutter Auth category plugin using the AWS Cognito provider.
packages.oneLiner: Amplify Flutter Auth plugin for AWS Cognito

useWhen: Need Cognito as backend for authentication
Want a single plugin that handles all auth flows
Targeting multiple platforms with a unified API
avoidWhen: Using a different backend like Firebase or Supabase
Needing fine‑grained control over low‑level auth APIs
Working in a pure Dart/CLI environment without Flutter

Built by AWS, tightly integrated with Cognito
Regular updates and bug fixes
Supports advanced flows like passwordless and OIDC
weaknesses: Requires AWS account and Cognito setup
Plugin size and dependencies may be heavy
Limited to Cognito, not generic OAuth

packages.name: qs_dart
packages.description: A query string encoding and decoding library for Dart. Ported from qs for JavaScript.
packages.oneLiner: A query string encoding and decoding library for Dart ported from JavaScript's qs.

explainer.whatItDoes: Encodes Dart maps into query strings and decodes query strings into nested maps and lists. It supports advanced features like dot notation, custom delimiters, different list formats, character sets, and safety limits.
useWhen: You need to encode complex, nested Dart maps into URL query strings.
You need to parse complex query strings with nested brackets or dot notation into maps.
You want parity with the JavaScript 'qs' library for API interoperability.
avoidWhen: You only need basic, flat query parameter manipulation covered by Dart's built-in Uri class.
strengths: Supports deeply nested maps and lists using bracket or dot notation.
Highly configurable options for charset encoding, duplicate handling, and depth limits.
Provides convenient Uri extensions for idiomatic Dart usage.
weaknesses: Adds an external dependency overhead for functionality partially handled by core libraries if query strings are completely flat.

packages.name: ordered_set
packages.description: A simple implementation of an Ordered Set for Dart that allows multiple items with the same priority.
packages.oneLiner: Ordered Set that keeps elements sorted and allows duplicates by priority.

explainer.whatItDoes: It stores items in order according to a comparator or a mapper function, permitting multiple items with the same priority. The set implements Iterable, so you can iterate in order with O(n) complexity.
useWhen: You need a sorted collection that accepts duplicate priorities
You want fast iteration over ordered elements
You need to query subsets by type or cache query results
avoidWhen: You only need a unique sorted set—use Dart's SplayTreeSet instead
You require persistence or async operations
strengths: Allows duplicate priorities
Simple API with static constructors
Iterable implementation for easy traversal
Supports query registration and caching
weaknesses: No built‑in persistence or async support
Not a full data‑structure library (no tree traversal APIs)

packages.name: expandable_page_view
packages.description: A PageView widget adjusting it's height to currently displayed page
packages.oneLiner: A PageView widget that automatically adjusts its height to the currently displayed page.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a drop-in replacement for the standard Flutter PageView that dynamically resizes its height to fit the content of the currently active page. It supports both fixed children and builder constructors, infinite looping, and programmatic page controllers.
useWhen: You have a PageView where pages have varying heights and you want the container to wrap the active page's height.
You need an infinite looping page view or carousel with dynamic heights.
avoidWhen: You need a standard fixed-height PageView filling the entire viewport.
You are looking for grid layouts or other non-page view scrollables.
strengths: Dynamically adjusts height based on visible pages and viewport fraction.
Supports infinite looping mode.
Compatible with standard PageView parameters and adds an ExpandablePageController.
weaknesses: Limited to page-snapping view functionality.
Height calculations can be complex with partial viewport fractions.

alternatives.name: carousel_slider
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a specialized carousel with indicators and built-in auto-play options rather than a raw PageView.

ExpandablePageView(

)

packages.name: amplify_analytics_pinpoint
packages.description: The Amplify Flutter Analytics category plugin using the AWS Pinpoint provider.
packages.oneLiner: AWS Pinpoint analytics plugin for Flutter

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a way to send analytics events to AWS Pinpoint from a Flutter app. It supports Android, iOS, Web, Windows, macOS, and Linux, and works with the Amplify Flutter ecosystem.

Your app targets multiple platforms including web and desktop
You already use Amplify Flutter for other services
avoidWhen: You are using a different analytics provider such as Firebase Analytics or Mixpanel
You only need simple event logging without a backend

packages.name: receive_sharing_intent
packages.description: A flutter plugin that enables flutter apps to receive sharing photos, text or url from other apps.
packages.oneLiner: Receives shared photos, videos, text, and files from other apps.

explainer.whatItDoes: Enables Flutter applications to receive sharing intents from other apps, such as photos, videos, text, URLs, and arbitrary file types. It supports Android intents and iOS Share extensions with automatic redirection or a custom compose UI.
useWhen: Your app needs to accept shared content or files sent from external apps like the system gallery or browser.
You want to build an iOS Share extension alongside your Android sharing setup.
avoidWhen: You only need to share data outward to other apps rather than receive incoming items.
strengths: Supports multiple file types including images, videos, text, URLs, and raw files.
Provides both stream-based listeners and initial media fetching.
Handles both Android intent filters and iOS Share extensions.
weaknesses: Requires manual native setup for both Android Manifest and iOS target extensions.
iOS setup requires Swift Package Manager configuration and creating a Share Extension target.

flags.label: Native setup

packages.name: strings
packages.description: Large collection of String functions aimed at extending the String class whilst providing safer methods for working with nullable Strings.
packages.oneLiner: Large collection of String functions extending the String class and supporting nullable Strings safely.

explainer.whatItDoes: The Strings package provides over 50 functions to complement the core String class. It extends String with helper methods and safely handles nullable strings without throwing errors.
useWhen: You need safe string operations that handle null values without throwing exceptions.
You want to use helper methods like affix removal, partition, and whitespace normalization.
avoidWhen: You need complex regular expression or Unicode normalization matching.
strengths: Never throws or returns errors on null inputs, making it robust.
Provides both static methods and String extension methods.
weaknesses: Matching is strictly literal, case-sensitive UTF-16 without regex support.

Strings.right(null, 4, pad: Pad.left);
'a normal string'.right(4);

packages.name: rate_limiter
packages.description: A pure dart package to apply useful rate limiting strategies on regular functions.
packages.oneLiner: Apply rate limiting strategies like debounce, throttle, and backoff to regular Dart functions.

explainer.whatItDoes: A pure Dart package that provides rate limiting strategies such as debounce, throttle, and backoff for regular functions. It allows you to convert existing functions or build new ones with built-in checks for pending execution, flushing, and cancellation.
useWhen: You need to debounce user input in a search box or text field.
You want to throttle rapid button clicks for game actions or API triggers.
You need to implement exponential backoff retry logic for network requests.
avoidWhen: You need complex stream-based reactive rate limiting rather than wrapping regular functions.
strengths: Simple extension methods for converting existing regular functions into debounced or throttled versions.
Deterministic testing support via package:clock and fakeAsync.

weaknesses: Limited to pure Dart functions rather than fully reactive stream transformations.

packages.name: fixed
packages.description: Fixed scale decimal numbers with mathematical operations, formatting and parsing.
packages.oneLiner: Fixed decimal numbers with a fixed scale, stored as BigInts, supporting math, formatting and parsing.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides a Fixed type that stores decimal numbers with a selectable number of decimal places using BigInts for precision. It offers arithmetic operators, comparison, formatting (including locale-aware) and parsing with error handling.
useWhen: Need precise decimal arithmetic for currencies or financial data
Require locale-aware formatting and parsing of decimal numbers
Want to avoid floating-point inaccuracies in calculations
avoidWhen: Working with arbitrary-precision decimals beyond a fixed scale
Needing binary floating-point math for performance-critical code

Built-in formatting and parsing with locale support

Consistent hash codes across different scales

No support for arbitrary-precision beyond the set scale
Requires Dart SDK 3.9.0 or higher

packages.name: charset

You need to detect the character encoding of byte data.
avoidWhen: You only need standard UTF-8 or ASCII encoding which is already built into Dart's core libraries.

packages.name: flutter_email_sender
packages.description: Allows send emails from flutter using native platform functionality.
packages.oneLiner: Allows sending emails from Flutter using native platform functionality.

Performance is critical for extremely large data sets.

Easy drop‑in replacement for existing ListView

Customization options are fewer than a full custom scroll implementation

packages.name: chopper

packages.oneLiner: An HTTP client generator for Dart and Flutter using source_gen.

You need to customize TLS or proxy settings for Dio

You only need basic HTTP/1.1 functionality

useWhen: You are building Dart Native Assets that require compiling a CMake project.
You need to configure custom CMake, Ninja, or Android NDK versions for your native builds via pubspec.yaml.
avoidWhen: Your project does not use Dart Native Assets or CMake.

hooks:

packages.name: youtube_explode_dart

useWhen: You want to fetch YouTube video metadata, captions, or comments without using the official YouTube Data API.

You are building a custom YouTube downloader or media application in Dart.

weaknesses: Relies on reverse-engineering and parsing raw page content, making it prone to breaking when YouTube updates its site.
Requires manual cleanup by closing the HTTP client to avoid halting the Dart process.

packages.name: dynatrace_flutter_plugin
packages.description: The Dynatrace Flutter plugin helps auto-instrument your Flutter app with Dynatrace OneAgent for Android and iOS. It also provides an API to add manual instrumentation.
packages.oneLiner: Auto-instrument Flutter apps with Dynatrace OneAgent for Android and iOS RUM.

useWhen: You need real user monitoring (RUM) and performance tracking through Dynatrace.
You want to automatically track crashes and errors across Android and iOS.
avoidWhen: You are using a different application performance monitoring (APM) platform like Firebase Crashlytics or Sentry.
Your target platforms do not include Android or iOS.
strengths: Automatic instrumentation of native and Flutter layers.
Comprehensive crash reporting and web request monitoring.
Supports modern routing solutions like go_router.
weaknesses: Requires manual configuration files (dynatrace.config.yaml) and native setup scripts.
Stricter requirements on minimum Android and iOS SDK versions.

import 'package:dynatrace_flutter_plugin/dynatrace_flutter_plugin.dart';

void main() => Dynatrace().start(MyApp());

packages.name: worker_manager
packages.description: The worker_manager allows you to manage CPU-intensive calculations across isolates

You want to reuse isolates instead of spawning a new one via compute every time

avoidWhen: You only need simple asynchronous I/O operations

Inter-isolate communication with ports

On web before isolate support, fallback executes similarly to compute method

packages.name: chalkdart
packages.description: Console/Logging text coloring and styling library for Dart. 'Terminal string styling done right' The default mode uses ANSI codes to style the text for Console/Terminal display. packages.name: val_latex

packages.name: excel_plus

useWhen: You need to read, write, or modify Excel (.xlsx or .xls) spreadsheets in Dart or Flutter
You are processing large workbooks and require low memory consumption and streaming parsers
You want a drop-in, faster replacement for the existing excel package
avoidWhen: You only need simple CSV handling and do not require Excel-specific features or formatting

packages.name: vector_map_tiles

useWhen: You are using flutter_map and need to render vector tiles instead of raster tiles
You want custom styling or dynamic themes for your maps from providers like Mapbox or Stadia Maps
avoidWhen: You are not using flutter_map
You prefer standard raster tile layers without vector styling features

alternatives.name: google_maps_flutter

packages.name: easy_refresh
packages.description: A flutter widget that provides pull-down refresh and pull-up load.
packages.oneLiner: A Flutter widget providing pull-down refresh and pull-up load for all scrollable widgets.

alternatives.name: auto_route

packages.oneLiner: Display native PDF views on Android and iOS from a path, asset, or cached URL.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides widgets to render native PDF views from various resources like local paths, asset bundles, or network URLs with built-in caching. Supports features such as zooming, swiping horizontally or vertically, jumping to specific pages, and password protection.
useWhen: You need to display PDF documents directly inside your Flutter UI on Android and iOS.
You need to load and cache remote PDFs from URLs automatically.
avoidWhen: You need robust web support (currently listed as 'soon' in the documentation).
You need advanced custom PDF rendering and manipulation logic in pure Dart rather than native platform views.
strengths: Supports loading from local paths, assets, and remote URLs with caching.
Native rendering performance using AndroidPdfViewer and PDFKit.
Customizable options for page swiping, zooming, night mode, and event callbacks.
weaknesses: Requires native configuration steps (like modifying Info.plist and Podfile on iOS).
Web support is not yet fully implemented.
Some options have platform-specific limitations (e.g., nightMode and pageSnap are Android-only).
explainer.setupNotes: Requires adding 'io.flutter.embedded_views_preview' to Info.plist and setting platform to at least iOS 11.0 in the Podfile. For Android with Proguard, you need to keep com.shockwave classes.

packages.name: zstandard
packages.description: Flutter plugin for fast Zstandard compression and decompression across native and WebAssembly platforms.
packages.oneLiner: Flutter plugin for fast Zstandard compression and decompression across native and WebAssembly.

explainer.whatItDoes: Provides native and WebAssembly integration for the Zstandard (zstd) compression algorithm via FFI. It allows compressing and decompressing byte data synchronously or asynchronously using extension methods or the main Zstandard class.
useWhen: You need fast data compression or decompression for local storage, transmission, or backups.
Your application targets multiple native platforms as well as the Web using WebAssembly.
avoidWhen: You only need simple string hashing or basic collections helpers without compression.
You are targeting Fuchsia where native support is not available.
strengths: Cross-platform support including Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, Linux, and Web via WebAssembly.
Offers both an object-oriented API and convenient extension functions on Uint8List.
weaknesses: Fuchsia is explicitly not supported.
Requires proper native integration configurations.
explainer.setupNotes: Add the dependency to pubspec.yaml; leverages native FFI and WebAssembly out of the box without complex manual linking steps for standard use.

packages.name: flutter_background
packages.description: Run apps in the background using foreground services on Android. Ideal for applications that require continuous operation, such as background data synchronization or messaging.
packages.oneLiner: Runs a Flutter app in the background on Android using a foreground service.

explainer.whatItDoes: The plugin starts a foreground Android service with a persistent notification to keep the Dart isolate alive. It also acquires a partial wake lock and can disable battery optimizations to allow continuous execution.
useWhen: continuous data sync or messaging that must run when the app is not visible
long‑running network connections that need to survive screen off
avoidWhen: iOS or cross‑platform projects that need background support on other platforms
scenarios where a foreground notification would be undesirable
strengths: Supports Android 14+ foreground‑service requirements
Handles wake lock and battery‑optimization permissions automatically
Simple API to enable/disable background execution
weaknesses: Android‑only; no iOS support
Requires a persistent notification, which may affect user experience
explainer.setupNotes: Add FOREGROUND_SERVICE permissions and a <service> entry with appropriate foregroundServiceType in AndroidManifest.xml; call FlutterBackground.initialize with notification config before enabling execution

useWhen: You need to use just_audio on Linux and Windows platforms.
You want to leverage media_kit's mpv backend for audio playback in a Flutter app.

packages.name: scroll_snap_list
packages.description: A Flutter widget that allows "snaping" event to an item at the end of user-scroll.
packages.oneLiner: A Flutter wrapper for ListView that snaps to items at the end of user-scroll.

explainer.whatItDoes: It wraps a ListView.builder to provide a snap-to-item behavior at the end of scrolling. It supports both horizontal and vertical scrolling directions, dynamic item sizing, opacity scaling, and custom positioning anchors.
useWhen: You need a horizontal or vertical list that snaps to items like a carousel or picker.
You want unrestricted scrolling combined with snapping without using rigid page views.
You need to trigger callbacks when specific items gain focus during a scroll.
avoidWhen: You require precise page-by-page snapping like a standard PageView with strict one-item bounds.
You are building complex custom physics-based scroll engines from scratch.
strengths: Supports both horizontal and vertical lists with unrestricted scroll behavior.
Provides dynamic item size and dynamic opacity scaling features.
Works out of the box with standard ListView builders and no external dependencies.
weaknesses: Requires providing a correct itemSize for proper calculation and snapping.
Tap detection on child items may conflict if items implement their own custom tap detectors, requiring manual key invocation.

alternatives.name: carousel_slider
alternatives.why_pick_it: Pick carousel_slider if you specifically need a card carousel with auto-play and pagination indicators rather than a general snap-to-item list wrapper.

Expanded(
  child: ScrollSnapList(
    onItemFocus: _onItemFocus,
    itemSize: 35,
    itemBuilder: _buildListItem,
    itemCount: data.length,
    reverse: true,
  ),
)

packages.name: mmkv
packages.description: An efficient, small mobile key-value storage framework developed by WeChat. Works on Android & iOS.
packages.oneLiner: An efficient, small mobile key-value storage framework.

explainer.whatItDoes: MMKV uses mmap to keep memory synced with files and protobuf to encode/decode values, providing fast key-value storage. It supports primitive types, strings, bytes, multi-process concurrency, and optional encryption.
useWhen: You need a high-performance key-value storage solution on mobile or desktop.
You require multi-process concurrent access to the same storage files.
avoidWhen: You require complex relational queries, which are better suited for a SQL database.
You need built-in reactive streams for data observation.
strengths: Extremely efficient memory and file synchronization via mmap.
Small binary footprint and lightweight dependencies.
Supports multi-process concurrency.
weaknesses: Must wait for MMKV initialization to finish before accessing instances.
Limited built-in data types compared to NoSQL document databases.
explainer.setupNotes: Call MMKV.initialize() in main() before running the app.

packages.name: squadron
packages.description: Multithreading and worker thread pool for Dart / Flutter, to offload CPU-bound and heavy I/O tasks to Isolate or Web Worker threads.
packages.oneLiner: Multithreading and worker thread pools for Dart and Flutter using Isolates and Web Workers.

explainer.whatItDoes: Squadron provides persistent worker pools and an abstraction layer to offload CPU-bound and heavy I/O tasks to background threads across platforms (Native Isolates and Web Workers). It handles type safety, task cancellation, streaming return types, and exception marshalling via code generation.
useWhen: You need to offload CPU-intensive tasks from the main thread without blocking UI performance.
You need persistent worker pools that stay alive across multiple tasks rather than spawning new isolates repeatedly.
You target both native (Dart VM) and browser platforms with a uniform multithreading API.
avoidWhen: Your app only requires simple one-off background tasks where `Isolate.run()` is sufficient and lightweight.
You want to avoid using code generation steps during development.
strengths: Cross-platform support for native Isolates and Web Workers (JS & WASM).
Persistent worker pools for handling frequent tasks efficiently.
Type-safe proxy generation and native Stream support from workers.
weaknesses: Requires code generation (`build_runner` and `squadron_builder`).
Requires manual worker lifecycle management (must call `stop()` to clean up background threads).
explainer.setupNotes: Add squadron to dependencies and squadron_builder / build_runner to dev_dependencies. Run build_runner to generate workers, and compile workers to JS/WASM for web targets.

packages.name: schemantic
packages.description: A lightweight library for type-safe data classes and runtime JSON Schemas, with built-in serialization and validation.
packages.oneLiner: Generate type-safe data classes and runtime JSON Schemas from abstract class definitions.

explainer.whatItDoes: Schemantic is a library that generates fully-typed Dart data classes and runtime-accessible JSON Schemas from simple abstract class definitions. It features built-in JSON serialization, runtime data validation against schemas, and support for recursive structures, union types, and custom types.
useWhen: You need to generate runtime JSON Schemas alongside immutable-style data classes from code definitions.
You want built-in runtime validation of JSON payloads against generated schemas.
You work with AI tools or structured output requirements that depend on strict JSON schemas.
avoidWhen: You are looking for state management solutions or UI widget component libraries.
You do not want to use code generation and build_runner in your workflow.
strengths: First-class runtime JSON schemas accessible from generated data classes.
Built-in serialization and runtime validation.
Supports recursive schemas and union types (AnyOf).
weaknesses: Requires build_runner and a separate builder package for code generation.
Adds an extra step to the development workflow for schema modifications.
explainer.setupNotes: Add schemantic, schemantic_builder, and build_runner as dependencies, then run build_runner to generate part files.

alternatives.name: freezed_annotation
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose freezed if you primarily want advanced union types, deep copying, and immutable data classes rather than runtime JSON schema generation.

packages.oneLiner: Extensible logging for Dart and Flutter based on the Android Timber library.

explainer.whatItDoes: Fimber provides extensible and structured logging for Dart and Flutter applications. It mimics the Android Timber library API by utilizing concepts like trees and planting logging trees to output debug, verbose, info, warn, and error messages.

packages.name: focus_detector
packages.description: Detects when your widget appears or disappears from the screen.

explainer.whatItDoes: FocusDetector provides callbacks to get notified every time a widget appears or disappears from the screen.
